record.context_brief: dimension bounds for k-orbit convex polytopes
record.original_question: For each integer k > 1, determine the smallest possible dimension bound N_k such that geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes exist only in dimensions below N_k, or at least improve the known general bounds for N_k.

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Determine N_k for every k or improve the bounds for it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex polytope of dimension $d$. A flag of $P$ is a maximal chain $F_{-1} < F_0 < F_1 < \cdots < F_{d-1} < F_d = P$ in the face lattice of $P$, where $F_i$ is an $i$-dimensional face (with $F_{-1} = \emptyset$). The Euclidean symmetry group $G(P)$ of $P$ is the group of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that map $P$ onto itself; it acts on the set $\mathcal{F}(P)$ of flags of $P$. The polytope $P$ is called geometrically $k$-orbit if the action of $G(P)$ on $\mathcal{F}(P)$ has exactly $k$ orbits.

For each integer $k > 1$, define
\[
N_k = \inf\{N \in \mathbb{N} \;:\; \text{there is no geometrically $k$-orbit convex polytope of dimension $\geq N$}\},
\]
with $N_k = \infty$ if geometrically $k$-orbit convex polytopes exist in arbitrarily high dimensions.

Determine $N_k$ for every integer $k > 1$, or, failing that, give the best possible upper and lower bounds on $N_k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of a collection of open problems on $k$-orbit polytopes (Problem 25 in that list). For $k=2$, a complete classification of geometrically two-orbit convex polytopes is known and they exist only in dimension 3, but general bounds $N_k$ for arbitrary $k>1$ have not been established in the literature that web searches surface. The problem appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.claim: The problem belongs to a curated list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Combinatorially two-orbit convex polytopes are isomorphic to one of a finite list, all 3-dimensional.
status_evidence.claim: For k=2 the geometric/combinatorial classification of convex k-orbit polytopes is fully resolved in dimension 3, but no general bound N_k for arbitrary k is established.
